ps.en: When Lin Mei's first paper was rejected, the reviewer's comment was brief: the conclusion was interesting, but the evidence did not [[stick]]. The words stung, yet they also [[stimulated|stimulate]] her to reopen the experiment she had closed months before. She refused to let one failure [[stir]] self-doubt — instead, she wanted to stir a real debate.
ps.zh: 林梅的第一篇论文被拒时，审稿人的意见只有一句：结论有意思，但证据站不住脚。这话很扎心，却也刺激她重新打开了数月前已经结束的实验。她拒绝让一次失败激起自我怀疑——相反，她想掀起一场真正的讨论。

ps.en: The journal [[stipulated|stipulate]] that every claim rest on published data, so Lin spent weeks cleaning her tables. From the noise she began to [[infer]] a pattern, and her [[inference]], though bold, was hard to ignore once the [[information]] was free for anyone to check. Even an [[influential]] critic wrote back, admitting the new [[approach]] deserved a second look.
ps.zh: 期刊规定每论断都必须建立在公开数据之上，于是林梅花了数周清理数据表。她从噪声中开始推断出一种模式；这个推断虽然大胆，但一旦资料任人核查，就再也无法被忽视。连一位有影响力的批评者也回信了，承认这种新思路值得再看一眼。

ps.en: "Never let an [[inferior]] instrument hide a good question," the critic told her. Under his [[influence]], Lin rebuilt the model, and her follow-up paper — the one the same journal now rushed into print — was proof that honest criticism can [[inform]] better science.
ps.zh: 「别让一件更差的工具遮住一个好问题，」那位批评者告诉她。在他的影响下，林梅重做了模型；而她的后续论文——正是那家期刊如今抢着刊出的那篇——证明了诚实的批评能让更好的科学得以传播。

ps.en: As an aide on the energy committee, Qian was [[conscious]] of one [[continual]] complaint: the old grid could not support [[continuous]] growth. When the [[congress]] opened its spring session, she drafted a modest proposal to [[connect]] every village clinic to a stable power source — the [[connection]] between electricity and survival was, to her, obvious.
ps.zh: 作为能源委员会的助理，钱某意识到一个反复出现的抱怨：老电网撑不起持续的增长。国会春季会议开幕时，她起草了一份不算张扬的提案，要把每个村诊所接上稳定的电源——在她看来，电与生存之间的联系显而易见。

ps.en: Her supervisor warned that any plan failing to [[conform]] to the budget would never win [[approval]]. Lobbyists, meanwhile, tried to [[confuse]] the public, spreading [[confusion]] about costs until even supporters fell silent. Yet Qian refused to [[confront]] them with anger; she answered every claim with a spreadsheet.
ps.zh: 她的上司警告说，任何不符合预算的方案都永远得不到批准。与此同时，游说集团试图混淆公众视听，散布关于成本的种种混乱说法，直到连支持者都沉默下去。但钱某拒绝用愤怒正面对抗他们；她用一张电子表格回应每一条说法。

ps.en: "The only [[appropriate]] standard is what villages can afford," she told the committee, and the [[apt]] phrase carried the vote. The bill passed with broad approval, and the chairman — who rarely [[approved|approve]] of anything — signed it with a smile. Qian [[continued|continue]] to watch the meters, certain that policy, like power, must travel the last mile.
ps.zh: 「唯一恰当的标准，是村子负担得起什么，」她对委员会说——这句贴切的话改变了投票。法案以广泛赞成获得通过，而那位难得认可任何事的主席，微笑着签了字。钱某继续盯着电表，她确信：政策像电力一样，必须走完最后一英里。

ps.en: For twenty years Dr. Han had [[examined|examine]] the coastline, and his maps told a plain story: the sea was rising. At town meetings he watched officials [[dismiss]] his charts with a smile, and the mayor once joked that a flood was a rumour invented to [[distract]] voters from real problems.
ps.zh: 二十年来，韩博士一直在细查这条海岸线，他的地图讲着一个直白的故事：海平面在上升。在镇上的会议上，他看着官员们笑着对他的图表不予理会；市长甚至开玩笑说，洪水不过是为了转移选民对真正问题的注意而编造的谣言。

ps.en: Then came the autumn storm. Water turned the main street into [[disorder]], and the crowd that gathered to watch soon had to [[disperse]] for their lives. Forty families were [[displaced|displace]] in a single night, their photographs and furniture piled on the steps of the museum where Han worked.
ps.zh: 秋天的风暴来了。大水把主街变成一片混乱，闻讯赶来看热闹的人群很快不得不四散逃命。一夜之间，四十户人家流离失所，他们的照片和家具堆放在韩博士工作的博物馆台阶上。

ps.en: The next morning Han refused to [[exaggerate]]: "a century of neglect," he said, "not a century storm." Some reporters tried to [[distort]] that into panic; others used the flood to [[mock]] science itself. But inside the museum he put the ruined maps on [[display]] and invited students to examine the mud — the slow [[evolution]] of a coastline written in sediment. Watching volunteers [[distribute]] blankets, he let himself believe the town could [[evolve]] into something wiser.
ps.zh: 第二天早上，韩博士拒绝夸大其词：「这是百年的忽视，」他说，「不是百年一遇的风暴。」有记者试图把他的话歪曲成恐慌渲染，也有人借这场洪水嘲笑科学本身。但在博物馆里，他把被毁的地图展出，请学生们细察那些淤泥——那是一部写在沉积物里的海岸线缓慢演变史。看着志愿者们分发毛毯，他让自己相信，这个镇子能演变成一个更明智的地方。

ps.en: When the old textile mill announced its [[modernization]], everyone expected a young engineer from the city. Instead they got Su, a woman of forty with a [[modest]] suitcase and no interest in speeches. Her task was to make the aging workshops [[modern]]; her [[mode]] of working was simple: walk the floor, listen, and change as little as possible.
ps.zh: 老纺织厂宣布现代化改造时，所有人都以为会来个城里的年轻工程师。来的却是苏——一个四十岁、提着不大的行李箱、对讲话毫无兴趣的女人。她的任务是让老旧车间现代化；她的工作方式很简单：下车间走、听、尽量少改动。

ps.en: The workers trusted no one; her [[predecessor]] had been a famous expert who never touched a machine. Su's [[preliminary]] report, when it came, ran to six pages, and its conclusion was that the old looms were [[preferable]] to any new [[model]] on the market. She asked only to [[modify]] three motors.
ps.zh: 工人们谁都不信；她的前任是个从不碰机器的名专家。苏的初步报告出来后只有六页，结论是：市场上的任何新式样都不如老织机可取。她只要求改装三台电机。

ps.en: Her [[moderate]] proposal offended the salesmen, whose [[prejudice]] favoured whatever was newest and most expensive. "You cannot [[predict]] failure," they warned. Su disagreed — you cannot predict anything without data — and in the [[preface]] to her final report she thanked the oldest weaver by name. A year later the mill doubled its output, and the salesmen, with quiet grace, changed their [[preference]].
ps.zh: 她这份温和适度的方案得罪了销售员——这些人的偏见是只认最新最贵的。“你预测不了失败，”他们警告说。苏并不认同——没有数据，什么都预测不了——在最终报告的前言里，她点名感谢了厂里年纪最大的织工。一年后，厂子产量翻了一倍，而那些销售员也心平气和地改变了自己的偏好。

a distorted picture 失真的图景
fam: distortion n. 扭曲；曲解
words.dif: distort 指使事实「变形、失实」；destroy 是「摧毁」，词根不同
words.pat: Social media can distort our view of what is normal.
words.patZh: 社交媒体会扭曲我们对「正常」的认知。

c: distract sb from 使某人从…分心
be distracted by 被…分散注意力
distract attention 转移注意力
fam: distraction n. 分心的事物；distracted adj. 心不在焉的
words.dif: distract 是「把注意力引开」；attract（吸引）、contract（收缩）、extract（抽出）同族异义，靠前缀区分
words.pat: Phone notifications constantly distract students from their reading.
words.patZh: 手机通知不断分散学生的阅读注意力。

c: the evolution of ……的演变
the theory of evolution 进化论
social evolution 社会演进
fam: evolve v. 进化；evolutionary adj. 进化的
words.dif: evolution 是名词「进化」；revolution 是「革命」，前缀 e- 与 re- 之差
words.pat: The evolution of the Internet has reshaped how we learn.
words.patZh: 互联网的演变重塑了我们的学习方式。

c: evolve from 由…进化而来
evolve into 演变成
gradually evolved 逐渐演化
fam: evolution n.；evolving adj. 不断演变的
words.dif: evolve 指「渐进演变」；revolve 是「旋转」，resolve 是「解决」，形近三兄弟
words.pat: Small family businesses can evolve into global companies.
words.patZh: 小型家族企业可以逐步发展成为全球性公司。

c: exaggerate the danger 夸大危险
greatly exaggerated 被严重夸大
exaggerate one's role 夸大了自己的作用
fam: exaggeration n. 夸大；exaggerated adj. 夸张的
words.dif: exaggerate 是「言过其实」；exacerbate 是「使恶化」，形近高频设项
words.pat: Reports of the product's failure have been greatly exaggerated.
words.patZh: 有关该产品失败的说法被严重夸大了。

c: examine sth closely 仔细检查
examine the evidence 审查证据
examine sb on sth 就…考问某人
fam: examination n. 检查；考试；examiner n. 考官
words.dif: examine 泛指「仔细检查」；inspect 侧重「官方巡查、验收」
words.pat: Researchers examined samples from over a thousand patients.
words.patZh: 研究人员检查了上千名患者的样本。

c: mock sb for sth 因…嘲笑
mock exam 模拟考试
make a mock of 嘲弄
fam: mocking adj. 嘲弄的；mockery n. 讥笑
words.dif: mock 是「嘲弄（可带模仿）」；mimic 只指「模仿」；laugh at 只是「发笑」
words.pat: Critics mocked the plan, yet it later proved its worth.
words.patZh: 批评者曾嘲笑这个方案，但后来它证明了自己的价值。

c: a mode of transport 交通方式
switch mode 切换模式
a mode of life 生活方式
fam: modal adj. 情态的；model n. 模型
words.dif: mode 是「运作方式、模式」；mood 是「情绪」，形近义异
words.pat: Walking is the healthiest mode of transport in crowded cities.
words.patZh: 在拥挤的城市里，步行是最健康的出行方式。

words.exam: 模（原）型；样（模）式；模范；典型；模仿
c: a role model 榜样
model sth on 以…为原型
an economic model 经济模型
fam: modelled / modeling（model - modelled - modelled） n. 相关延伸
words.dif: model on 是「以…为榜样仿制」；mould 是「塑造（性格、形状）」
words.pat: She modeled her teaching style on her favourite professor.
words.patZh: 她以最喜欢的教授为榜样来塑造自己的教学风格。

c: moderate exercise 适度运动
moderate views 温和的观点
moderate prices 适中的价格
fam: moderation n. 适度；moderately adv.
words.dif: moderate 是「适度、温和」；modern 是「现代的」，形近义异
words.pat: Moderate exercise, done daily, beats intense workouts done rarely.
words.patZh: 每天坚持适度运动，胜过偶尔剧烈运动。

c: modern society 现代社会
modern technology 现代科技
modern history 近代史
fam: modernize v. 现代化；modernization n.；modernity n. 现代性
words.dif: modern 泛指「近代以来的」；contemporary 指「同一时代的、当下的」
words.pat: Modern medicine has doubled average life expectancy.
words.patZh: 现代医学使人均寿命翻了一番。

c: the modernization of ……的现代化
agricultural modernization 农业现代化
drive modernization 推进现代化
fam: modern adj. → modernize v. → modernization n.
words.dif: modernization 是「现代化进程」；modernism 是「现代主义（文艺流派）」
words.pat: The modernization of the railway network cut travel times in half.
words.patZh: 铁路网的现代化使出行时间缩短了一半。

words.exam: 谦虚的；适度的；不太大的
c: be modest about 对…很谦虚
a modest income 不高的收入
a modest proposal 温和的建议
fam: modesty n. 谦虚
words.dif: modest 是「谦逊、不张扬」；humble 还可指「出身卑微、地位低下」，语义更宽
words.pat: She was modest about her success, crediting her whole team.
words.patZh: 她对成功表现谦逊，把功劳归于整个团队。

c: modify the plan 修改方案
be modified by 被…修饰
modify one's behaviour 改变自己的行为
fam: modification n. 修改；modifier n. 修饰语
words.dif: modify 是「部分修改使其更好」；change 是不分方向的「改变」
words.pat: The design was modified to reduce production costs.
words.patZh: 为降低生产成本，设计被作了修改。

words.exam: 前辈；前任；（被取代的）原有事物
c: one's immediate predecessor 直接前任
the predecessor of ……的前身
compared with its predecessor （相关常用表达）
fam: pre-（在前）+ decess（离开）；successor n. 继任者
words.dif: predecessor 是「前任（人或旧物）」；successor 是「继任者」，方向相反
words.pat: The new system is twice as fast as its predecessor.
words.patZh: 新系统的速度是其前代的两倍。

c: predict that... 预测…
it is predicted that... 据预测…
accurately predict 准确预测
fam: prediction n. 预测；predictable adj. 可预测的；unpredictable
words.dif: predict 泛指基于分析的「预测」；forecast 多指「天气、经济的预报」
words.pat: Economists predict that growth will slow next year.
words.patZh: 经济学家预测明年增速将放缓。

c: the preface to a book 一本书的序言
in the preface 在前言中
write a preface 作序
fam: pre-（在前）+ face（说）；prefatory adj. 序言的
words.dif: preface 多为作者自序；foreword 多由他人作，考试较少细分
words.pat: In the preface, the author explains why he wrote the book.
words.patZh: 作者在前言中说明了自己为何写这本书。

c: be preferable to 比…更可取（用 to）
a preferable alternative 更优的选择
far preferable 好得多
fam: prefer v. → preferable adj. → preferably adv.
words.dif: preferable to 用 to 不用 than；prefer A to B 是同一结构
words.pat: Prevention is always preferable to cure.
words.patZh: 预防总是比治疗更可取。

c: a preference for 对…的偏爱
in preference to 优先于
give preference to 优先考虑
fam: prefer v. → preference n. → preferential adj. 优惠的
words.dif: preference 是「个人偏爱」；priority 是「客观上的优先级」
words.pat: Employers show a growing preference for practical experience.
words.patZh: 雇主越来越偏爱实践经验。

c: prejudice against 对…的偏见
without prejudice 不带偏见
racial prejudice 种族偏见
fam: pre-（预先）+ judice（判断）；prejudiced adj. 有偏见的
words.dif: prejudice 是「先入为主的成见（多负面）」；bias 是「系统性偏向」，可中性
words.pat: We should judge candidates on merit, free from prejudice.
words.patZh: 我们应该不受偏见影响，凭实力评判候选人。

c: preliminary results 初步结果
a preliminary investigation 初步调查
preliminary talks 预备会谈
fam: preliminarily adv.；prelim n. 预赛（口语）
words.dif: preliminary 指「正式步骤前的准备性」；primary 是「首要的」，同前缀不同义
words.pat: Preliminary findings suggest the treatment is safe.
words.patZh: 初步研究结果表明该疗法是安全的。
